previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of T2 paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, and prior episodes of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) was admitted with acute confusion, severe headache, and transient bilateral vision loss. She had been experiencing worsening chronic pain and was found to have markedly elevated blood pressure. Brain imaging, including CT and MRI, confirmed PRES with characteristic white matter changes. Urinalysis showed signs of infection, and culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, indicating a complicated urinary tract infection. Antibiotics were initially withheld due to atypical presentation but were started with ertapenem after lack of mental status improvement. Blood pressure was controlled with captopril and then transitioned to lisinopril. A PICC line was placed to complete a 7-day course of IV antibiotics at home. Her mental status normalized, and she was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotic administration and neurology follow-up to evaluate for sympathetic dysregulation.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with paraplegia (T2), neurogenic bladder requiring frequent 
self-cath, and multiple MDR resistant UTIs who presented on 
___ for evaluation of a sacral wound.

# Hypotension: Patient developed asymptomatic hypotension 
requiring two medical ICU transfers.  The first was concerning 
for sepsis given fever for which patient was started on 
broad-spectrum antibiotics (see below).  The second medical ICU 
transfer was correlated with getting narcotics, so the decision 
was made not to administer narcotics for the rest of this 
admission.  

# Hyponatremia: Patient developed progressive hyponatremia to 
nadir of Na 124. This was concerning for hypervolemic 
hyponatremia in the setting of receiving 7L IVF for hypotension. 
The renal team was consulted and also felt that hypervolemia was 
the most likely etiology.  The patient was diuresed with IV 
lasix and fluid-restricted with improvement in Na to 135 at the 
time of discharge.

# Urinary tract infection: In the setting of hypotension (see 
above), urine culture was sent and grew pan-sensitivie E. coli. 
The patient was initially started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, 
which was narrowed to PO Ciprofloxacin prior to discharge to 
complete a 10 day course. 

# Respiratory status:  The patient has baseline restrictive 
ventilatory defect for which she was continued on her home 
Ipratropium and albuterol.  On ___, the patient endorsed 
increased shortness of breath in the setting of receiving ___ 
IV fluids for hypotension in the medical ICU. Chest X-Ray showed 
increased pulmonary edema so patient received low dose IV lasix 
with improvement in respiratory status back to baseline 
(intermittent supplemental O2 at home).

# Sacral decubitus ulcer: The surgery team was consulted, and 
they debrided the ulcer twice on ___ and ___ for better 
granulation tissue/healing (not for infection).  The wound care 
team was consulted and recommended dry gauze packing BID. 
 
# Right Femur Fracture: Occured ___ deemed to be 
non-operative. Patient was continued on Lovenox and leg brace.

# Chronic Pain: The patient's pain was managed with standing 
Tylenol, lidocaine patches as well as her home gabapentin and 
baclofen.  Because the patient experienced hypotension in the 
setting of narcotic use, the decision was made not to administer 
further narcotics during this admission.  No pain medications 
were prescribed during this admission. 

# Anxiety/depression: Continued home Clonazapam, Citalopram, 
Trazodone.
  
# Neurogenic bladder/Paraplegia: Continued home oxcarbazepine, 
baclofen, sucralfate
oxybutynin.
